_comments: SALES' FIRST ACTION. The hourly activity sync (S-US10 #120), fired by the ScheduledJob row under
`DriverClass` is a ClassFactory key, not a display name: `@RegisterClass(BaseAction,
resolves to, and `LoadSyncActivitiesAction()` in the server bootstrap is what keeps that
registration from being tree-shaken away. Get either wrong and the action exists in metadata, is
scheduled, fires on time, and does nothing -- with no error anywhere.
SHAPE COPIED FROM ORDERS deliberately (`Orders.GenerateInvoice`): Type Custom, CodeApprovalStatus
Approved, Status Active, params as an `MJ: Action Params` related collection with `@parent:ID`.
Sales had no action of its own, so there was no local precedent -- and a second convention for the
same thing in one workspace is worse than following the one that exists.
WHAT THIS ACTION DOES NOT DECIDE: which source it reads. That is the process-wide factory
(`SetActivitySourceFactory`), whose default is an EMPTY fixture. So this row is safe to ship Active
-- it runs the whole pipeline hourly and writes nothing until a deployment hands it a real source.
Putting the source choice in a metadata field would bury the one decision that needs a human who
has confirmed the tenant's Exchange Application Access Policy.

fields.Name: Sync Activities
fields.Description: Pull messages and calendar items for every Active Microsoft365 sync connection, keep only those involving a known contact, and file them as Activities against the deal they belong to. Idempotent: re-running over the same window writes nothing new.
fields.UserPrompt: Run the hourly activity sync for the sales app.

fields.Name: Limit
fields.Description: How many items to pull per mailbox per run. Not merely a performance dial: MJ's GetMessages contract has no date filter, so a run fetches the most recent N and discards what it has already seen — which means anything older than the Nth newest message since the last run is missed and never retried. Raise it or run more often for a busy mailbox. See D-17.
